# Python dependency set for the `report-manager` job in
# .github/workflows/ci.yml. Nothing else installs this file.
#
# Why it exists instead of just `pip install -r requirements.txt`:
#
#   * the repo-root requirements.txt pins sentence-transformers, which drags in
#     torch — gigabytes of wheels — for an embedder that nothing under test
#     ever constructs. apps/api/embed_models/factory.py imports it lazily
#     inside create_embedder(), so the import graph the tests touch never
#     reaches it.
#   * apps/report-manager/requirements.txt is worse: it pins paddleocr==2.8.1,
#     whose single process peaks around 6.4 GB RSS. Production is already
#     Tesseract-only (apps/api/Dockerfile sets OCR_DISABLE_PADDLE=true), so CI
#     installing paddle would be minutes and gigabytes spent on a code path the
#     deployed image does not take.
#
# Every entry below was arrived at empirically, starting from an empty 3.11
# venv and adding only what an actual pytest collection error demanded. The
# version specifiers mirror the ones already in the repo-root requirements.txt
# so CI never resolves a wheel a developer's environment would not.
#
# When a test starts importing something new, add it here — do not "fix" it by
# switching this job to the full requirements.txt.

# Parser and OCR dependencies the apps/report-manager tests import, plus pytest
# itself. That file in turn includes apps/api/requirements-embedded-report.txt,
# so CI exercises the same wheel set the api image ships.
-r ../apps/report-manager/requirements-dev.txt

# scripts/kb_parsers/test_{docx,pptx,pdf,html,markdown}_parser.py build real
# fixture documents in tmp_path and parse them with the real libraries, so
# these are import-time requirements of the test modules, not optional extras.
python-docx>=1.1.2
python-pptx>=1.0
pdfminer.six>=20240706
beautifulsoup4>=4.12
PyYAML>=6.0

# scripts/kb_parsers/test_factory_default.py imports kb_backends.pgvector AND
# kb_backends.chroma_cloud eagerly — it monkey-patches both constructors to
# prove the factory default is pgvector without connecting to anything — so
# both backends' import-time dependencies must resolve even though that test
# instantiates neither. psycopg needs the `pool` extra specifically:
# apps/api/kb_backends/pgvector.py imports psycopg_pool at module scope.
#
# test_pgvector_reusable_embeddings.py does construct a real PgVectorBackend
# and open connections, against the postgres service container the
# report-manager job declares, so these two are runtime requirements as well
# as import-time ones. `pgvector` also brings numpy, which is what
# register_vector hands embeddings back as.
psycopg[binary,pool]>=3.2.10,<3.4
pgvector>=0.3.6,<0.5
chromadb==1.4.0
